anchor.title: Walks down the stairs alone without holding on.

items.title: Catches a ball with just their hands in the air.
Can use scissors correctly with the thumb up.
Hops on one foot for 2 seconds.
Jumps backward.
Catches a bounced ball.
Forms playdough shapes (like an animal).
Takes steps using heel-to-toe motion.
Rides a tricycle.
Recognizes things that are the same and when they're a bit different, like an item that is out of place.
Understands when something is long or short.
Holds up 5 fingers to mean 5.
Counts from 1 to 30.
Acts out stories following a clear order.
Mixes real and fantasy topics when talking.
Names simple shapes like a circle, triangle, or square.
Sorts things by their shape, like finding all the triangular blocks.

anchor.title: Uses sentences with at least five words.

items.title: Says words that rhyme, like cat-hat.
Gives instructions.
Talks about news from newspapers, radio, TV, or other sources.
Can have a chat using four sentences in a row.
Tells a story.
Most people understand them when they speak.
Adapts speech tone for different situations (asks questions with rising tone, shows surprise).
Talks about their day.

anchor.title: Can say who their friends are among kids they know.

items.title: Puts on a shirt without buttons.
Cuts food with a kid's knife with supervision.
Can undo a big button on their clothes.
Solves problems with other kids, like sharing toys or taking turns.
Cooperates with other kids, like working together to achieve something.
Pours water from a pitcher into a cup with both hands.
Identifies situations and activities they they enjoy.
Puts their pants on.
